description: Two-panel composite figure of transmission electron microscopy. (a) and (b) are dark-field (DF) TEM micrographs, each carrying a selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern as an inset (top-right of each panel). (a) is labelled "723 K/6 h" and (b) "723 K/9 h" in white block text at bottom-left; each has a 50 nm scale bar at bottom-right. Both DF images show a dense, uniformly dispersed field of fine bright κ-carbide particles in a darker matrix, with no visible grain-boundary or matrix-directed alignment; the bright speckle in (b) appears slightly coarser and brighter than in (a). The two SAED insets are visually identical in labelling: bright reflections annotated in yellow as 020, 011, 002, 010 and 001, with the beam-direction annotation [100]γ // [100]κ at the bottom of the inset, indicating a cube-on-cube orientation relationship between austenite and κ-carbide. No diffraction indices are given in white. Taken together the panels show that intragranular κ-carbides remain present and coherent in the 0.04Nb steel after aging at 723 K at both 6 h and 9 h, and that the longer treatment coarsens rather than re-nucleates them. No numeric particle size or volume-fraction value is printed in the figure itself.

subfigures.description: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 h, with a 50 nm scale bar and the label "723 K/6 h". The field shows a dense dispersion of fine bright κ-carbide particles in a darker matrix. A SAED inset (top-right) shows spots labelled 020, 011, 002, 010, 001 and the annotation [100]γ // [100]κ.

Dark-field TEM micrograph of the 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 9 h, with a 50 nm scale bar and the label "723 K/9 h". The bright κ-carbide speckle appears slightly coarser/brighter than in (a). The SAED inset carries the same yellow-indexed spots (020, 011, 002, 010, 001) and the same [100]γ // [100]κ annotation.

observations.observation: The figure consists of two dark-field TEM micrographs, each with an SAED pattern inset at its top-right corner.
Panel (a) is labelled "723 K/6 h" in white block text at the bottom-left and carries a 50 nm scale bar at the bottom-right.
Panel (b) is labelled "723 K/9 h" in white block text at the bottom-left and carries a 50 nm scale bar at the bottom-right.
Both SAED insets show diffraction spots annotated in yellow as 020, 011, 002, 010 and 001, with the beam-direction annotation [100]γ // [100]κ printed at the bottom of the inset.
Both dark-field images show a dense, homogeneous dispersion of fine bright particles in a darker matrix, with no obvious banding or preferred alignment.
The bright particle speckle in (b) (9 h) appears slightly coarser and brighter than in (a) (6 h), consistent with particle growth, though the difference is subtle at the supplied resolution.
The figure is TEM characterization of intragranular κ-carbides in the aged 0.04Nb steel at 723 K for (a) 6 h and (b) 9 h.
The two panels are identified in the citing text as TEM dark-field (DF) images of κ-carbides.
After aging for 6 and 9 h, the volume fraction of κ-carbides increases to 18.7 and 19.5 vol%, respectively.
The average κ-carbide size increases to 7 and 9 nm for the 6 h and 9 h aging treatments, respectively.
The citing text concludes that prolonging the aging treatment time promotes κ-carbide growth in the Nb-containing steel.
